speaker: Vale of White Horse District Council
quote: Motion passed with amendments: solar should go on non-agricultural land first and avoid high-grade farmland; local shared ownership or benefit schemes and biodiversity gain; the Vale should not bear NSIP harms while benefits leave the district; cumulative impact with Botley West, the West Oxfordshire Energy Park and the reservoir must be considered.
source_label: Vale of White Horse: Cearn motion documents, 21 October 2026
note: The motion asks for a letter to Defra, but the decision-maker for Cearn is the DESNZ Secretary of State.

speaker: Vale of White Horse District Council
quote: Written answers: Cearn is decided by the Secretary of State; the council is working with the Oxfordshire Association of Local Councils so parishes can input; officers are taking a programme-wide approach to cumulative impacts through the Joint Local Plan.
source_label: Vale of White Horse: written responses to questions, 21 October 2026

speaker: Oxfordshire County Council
role: Statutory consultee; highways and flood authority
quote: No Cabinet decision, highways response or motion on Cearn found.
note: Watch for the scoping response from OCC as highways and flood authority.

speaker: CPRE Oxfordshire
quote: Monitoring Cearn and attended initial events; no formal position yet. Its 2023 position paper wants Grades 1, 2 and 3a land avoided, rooftops and brownfield first, and treats cumulative impact as critical.
